ai.definition: Hyper-Automated RPA Agents are AI-driven software tools that can observe user behavior on digital interfaces and automate complex workflows across multiple applications without the need for explicit programming or APIs.
ai.howItWorks: These agents leverage Computer Vision (CV) to recognize UI elements and actions, then use Language Models (LMs), often Large Language Models (LLMs), to understand context and perform tasks. They can mimic human interactions such as clicking, typing, and scrolling without needing detailed scripts or API access.
ai.problemSolved: They address the challenge of automating intricate workflows that span multiple applications where traditional RPA tools may struggle due to lack of API support or complex UIs.
ai.manufacturing: Not applicable; these are software-based solutions developed through coding and machine learning training processes.
ai.buildProcess: Development involves training models on large datasets, integrating CV and NLP technologies, and continuous testing across various application environments.
ai.costDrivers: Initial development costs for AI model training, ongoing maintenance of the AI algorithms, and integration with existing systems are key cost factors. Licensing fees for pre-trained LLMs can also be significant.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: Expected to grow as more enterprises adopt RPA solutions, driven by increasing complexity in digital workflows and demand for efficiency.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by industry; compliance with data privacy laws (like GDPR) and security standards is crucial. Specific regulations around AI usage are still evolving.
ai.risks: Data privacy concerns, potential bias in AI models, integration challenges with existing systems, and the risk of over-reliance on automation leading to job displacement.
ai.profitability: High potential for profitability as businesses seek cost savings through increased efficiency. However, high initial investment can be a barrier for smaller companies.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more advanced AI capabilities, better cross-platform compatibility, and enhanced security features.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to computational requirements during training but not significant in deployment.

glossary.def: Robotic Process Automation, a type of software technology that automates business processes.
Large Language Model, a class of AI model used for natural language processing tasks.
Computer Vision, the field of AI concerned with enabling machines to interpret and understand visual information from the world.

subsystems.name: Perception layer
subsystems.role: works out what is on screen and which element means what.

subsystems.name: Planning layer
subsystems.role: turns a goal such as 'process this invoice' into an ordered set of actions.

subsystems.name: Action layer
subsystems.role: performs the clicks, keystrokes and calls the plan requires.

subsystems.name: Orchestration
subsystems.role: runs many jobs reliably in the background.

subsystems.name: Knowledge and memory
subsystems.role: keeps the business context the agent needs between steps and runs.

subsystems.name: Governance and oversight
subsystems.role: keeps the automation auditable, safe and correctable.

buildSteps.title: Find and rank candidate processes
buildSteps.detail: Analyse system event logs and recordings of real staff work to find repetitive, high-volume, rule-bound tasks. Score each on volume, variability and the cost of an error.

buildSteps.title: Record and model the process
buildSteps.detail: Capture the full path through the applications involved, including branches such as 'field missing'. Write it as a state machine with a defined success condition and a defined set of exceptions.

buildSteps.title: Build the perception layer
buildSteps.detail: Ground each UI element using a combination of the accessibility tree, OCR text and image matching. Store several fallback locators per element, because layouts change and single selectors break.

buildSteps.title: Define the agent's action space
buildSteps.detail: Give the model a narrow, typed list of tools — click, type, read table, call API, send for approval — rather than free control of the desktop. This is what makes behaviour testable and reviewable.

buildSteps.title: Ground and evaluate the model
buildSteps.detail: Supply the procedure, screenshots and worked examples. Replay dozens of recorded sessions and measure step-level accuracy, not just end-to-end pass rate, so failures can be localised.

buildSteps.title: Run it in a locked-down worker
buildSteps.detail: Execute inside a container or virtual machine with injected credentials, no broad network access, and all input and output logged.

buildSteps.title: Design the failure path first
buildSteps.detail: Set confidence thresholds below which the agent pauses, screenshots the state and asks a human to finish. Feed those corrections back as training and test cases.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and monitor
buildSteps.detail: Roll out behind a queue with concurrency limits, then watch for drift: when an application updates its interface, detection rates drop and locators must be re-grounded.

prerequisites.why: decades of screen-scraping and input-synthesis code already handle the mechanical execution.
they allow an agent to identify buttons, forms and tables without a bespoke selector for every one.
they expose element roles and names, far more stable than pixel coordinates.
agents still lose track over dozens of steps and cannot always tell that they have gone wrong.

prerequisites.tech: Enterprise identity, secrets and audit controls
prerequisites.why: an agent holding staff credentials needs scoped access and a complete action trail to be acceptable to auditors.

pathway.milestone: unattended bots handling structured, high-volume tasks such as invoice entry and record matching, with vision-based locators as backup
pathway.unlocks: measurable labour savings on narrow, stable processes and a base of logged process data.

pathway.milestone: LLM-planned agents that complete whole back-office workflows across several applications, pausing for human approval at defined checkpoints
pathway.unlocks: automation of tasks that were too variable to script, plus a much shorter build time per process.

pathway.milestone: self-healing automations that re-ground themselves after an application interface changes
pathway.unlocks: lower maintenance cost, which is currently the dominant cost of running an RPA estate.

pathway.milestone: agents that discover and propose their own automations from observed work, and hand tasks to each other across departments
pathway.unlocks: process improvement as a continuous background function rather than a project.
